memory_update.text: AXTI should be retained as the cleanest US-listed underfollowed InP substrate candidate, but survival to later layers depends on proving AI/datacenter optical pull-through, not merely optical-communications cyclicality.
TSEM should be retained as the silicon-photonics foundry reference asset; despite large-cap size, its exposure is unusually direct and useful for mapping PH18/SiPho ecosystem dependencies.

MKSI is an indirect shadow beneficiary candidate at the photonics/process-tool layer; evidence gap is product-level revenue tied specifically to laser, PIC, or optical-interconnect manufacturing capacity.

LWLG is a speculative shadow candidate because Tower PH18 validation creates a path, but production revenue, qualification, reliability, and yield evidence are not yet strong enough for a higher-confidence label.

The optical-interconnect materials node should be split in later layers into at least four subnodes: InP substrates, laser/epitaxy tools, silicon-photonics foundry process capacity, and modulator/material platforms.

node: Optical interconnect materials: indium phosphide substrates, laser wafers, silicon photonics foundry capacity, and optical-engine inputs
summary: Layer 1B expansion found a plausible two-lane universe around the upstream optical-interconnect bottleneck. Reference/context lane: Tower Semiconductor is the clearest US-listed silicon-photonics foundry proxy; Lumentum, Coherent, Fabrinet, Broadcom, NVIDIA networking, and Arista remain context anchors but are intentionally not allowed to crowd the discovery lane. Underfollowed lane: AXT is the most direct US-listed InP substrate exposure; MKS is an indirect photonics/process-tool and subsystem supplier; Lightwave Logic is a speculative shadow candidate tied to EO polymer modulators and Tower PH18 validation. The core chokepoint question is whether AI networking demand moves scarcity upstream from module assembly into qualified InP substrates, laser/epitaxy capacity, silicon-photonics process capacity, modulators, metrology, and photonics manufacturing tools.
